newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan gold traders see more near-term price dips.
newsitem.headline: Japan gold traders see more near-term price dips.

text.p: Gold prices are expected to dip further in the near term as bearish factors continue to overhang the metal, which fell to a four-and-a-quarter-year low of $334.00 an ounce in New York on Friday, traders said on Monday.

Lingering concerns over possible gold sales by European central banks, low inflation in the U.S. and slack physical gold demand in Asian countries such as Japan were behind gold's feeble performance, they said.
"Spot gold looks vulnerable to further tests to the downside risk as physical gold demand in Asia, excluding India...has not been very good," a precious metal industry source said.
"Spot gold may probe the downside at around $330 per ounce in the near future as Indian gold demand is seen seasonally weak heading into the monsoon months," he said.
Traders said Australian producers have been selling gold for hedging purposes in recent days in anticipation of a further slide in spot gold prices.
Spot gold was quoted at $334.90/335.30 per ounce at 0581 GMT, against $334.30/80 in New York on Friday.
TOCOM benchmark gold was off eight yen per gram in afternoon trade, standing at 1,225 yen per gram.
One factor seen determining near-term direction in the price of gold is the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Tuesday and Wednesday this week, traders said.
"If the FOMC leaves interest rates unchanged, as is widely expected, U.S. stock markets may continue to climb and exert downward pressure on gold," a bullion house official said.
"Gold may test around $326 per ounce," he said.
Another trader said overseas funds have been building short positions since gold prices were at around $340 per ounce based on a perception that the FOMC would leave interest rates unchanged.
A price of below $330 would likely trigger overseas funds to cover their short positions, he said.
